assumptions: m in {2,3,4}, b_j in {0..3}, J <= 3 (last coefficient nonzero): 189 rules
unary starts n <= 200; representations for n <= 3000
meta.falsification: A rule with sum b < m and an infinite derivation, a rule with sum b >= m terminating from all n <= 200 with no glider, or a radix-order inversion.
meta.hypothesis: H-C02-1: the rule terminates from every unary start iff sum_j b_j < m (emergent base r > 1, r the positive root of sum_j b_j r^j = m); otherwise some start produces a periodic glider. H-C02-2: for terminating rules, n < n' implies rep(n) < rep(n') in radix order.
meta.methodology: Batch-firing upward sweep. After level k is processed the future depends only on the window (c_{k+1}, ..., c_{k+J}), and the window map is monotone; a window W with an entry >= m that is later dominated componentwise (periodic glider if equal) certifies infinitely many firings. Radix order = compare length, then digits from the top.
meta.question: Which carry rules turn unary numerals into finite normal forms, what is the emergent base, and are the resulting representations ordered like ordinary numerals?
meta.title: Carry-rule survey: termination criterion, glider certificates and emergent bases

summary: 189 carry rules; 31 terminate from all unary n <= 200, all with sum b < m; H-C02-1 violations: 0
every non-terminating rule has a certificate (periodic glider or monotone pumping): True
H-C02-2 (radix monotonicity) violations among terminating rules: 0
